input.description: Restructure the contribution around an inference-isolating factorial design rather than around 'context vs. no context'. Arms on one base model and one KG, all with matched example counts, matched total supervision tokens, matched prompt template and matched optimization steps: (A) isolated triple/path; (B) target + passage-derived context triples; (C) target + an equal-length set of irrelevant/random triples; (D) target + relevance-selected context triples at the same token count as B. The primary claim becomes the causal contrast B vs. C (does relevance matter?), with A vs. C as a manipulation check for any extra-context effect and B vs. D testing whether selection helps. Includes a no-fine-tuning LLM reference point, since prior evidence shows imprecise context can fall below the no-context baseline.
input.expected_benefit: Makes the headline result attributable: if B beats C, the gain is due to passage-context relevance; if B only matches C, the original idea is refuted cleanly rather than ambiguously. The equal-length irrelevant arm also protects against the finding that long/irrelevant context can degrade or be ignored.
input.experimental_difficulty_basis: Requires careful construction of the irrelevant-triple arm (length- and structure-matched but semantically unrelated), token accounting across arms, and multiple seeds to distinguish a real effect from noise; the training runs themselves are conventional fine-tuning jobs.
input.implementation_difficulty_basis: No new model components are needed beyond an isolated-triple baseline that already exists; the work is mainly data construction (context arms) and budget accounting.
input.main_risk: The irrelevant-triple control may itself change behaviour (e.g. teach 'ignore context'), and exact token matching can force unnatural truncation that differs from how the context arm would naturally be used. Pre-registration and a token-bucket analysis are needed to guard against post-hoc arm construction.
input.potential_novelty: Hedged: the context family is crowded, so the novelty is not 'adding context' but the controlled causal test under matched budgets with an equal-length irrelevant arm in a training-time KGQA setting. No retrieved study performs this; if the effect is null or attributable to quantity, that is itself a publishable negative result.
required_baselines: NSM-style intermediate supervision (reproduced under the same budget)
input.technical_mechanism: Keep the supervision pipeline unchanged; only vary what accompanies each target triple/path. For each target, materialise four context versions with identical serialization and token counts where possible. Enforce matched example counts and matched total supervision tokens by truncating or padding the context field (padding drawn from the irrelevant pool for arm C), and log exact token counts per arm. Analyse results as a within-example paired comparison across arms plus a between-seed variance estimate.
input.title: Make the matched-budget context-relevance ablation the primary experiment
input.why_differs: DrKGC warns about long-context noise but treats subgraph compactness as a design choice with no matched control; SG-RAG MOT varies context scope without a no-context or equal-length-irrelevant arm; the IKG/KGSweetSpot study compares triple vs. path representations and relevance filtering only in prompts for multiple-choice QA, with no training and no budget matching. This modification is the first to make budget-matched relevance the object of study in training-time KG supervision.

input.description: Define an explicit relevance-selection operator for co-passage triples instead of taking all of them. Candidate operators: (i) graph-distance/connectivity to the target path or question entities; (ii) relation-type matching against the target relation; (iii) a learned scorer trained on whether a context triple helps answer the question; (iv) passage-position proximity. Treat the number of retained triples as an explicit precision/recall budget and report an ablation curve over context size, since the IKG study shows scope trades recall against precision.
input.expected_benefit: Directly addresses the demonstrated failure mode that imprecise KG context can degrade performance below the no-context baseline, and turns the underexplored 'which co-passage triples' question into a measurable design axis.
input.experimental_difficulty_basis: Requires an ablation curve over context size and selection operators (several training runs), plus a relevance annotation proxy; manageable but not a single-run study.
input.implementation_difficulty_basis: Simple heuristics (i), (ii), (iv) are easy, but a learned relevance scorer needs labels for 'helpful context triple', which must be constructed or bootstrapped.
input.main_risk: The selection operator may itself be the main effect, turning the contribution into 'better retrieval' — which overlaps heavily with existing subgraph-retrieval work (GNN-RAG, DrKGC, ToG-3) and with the IKG relevance-filtering study. The overlap must be argued by stage (training supervision vs. inference retrieval) and by the budget-matched ablation.
input.potential_novelty: Hedged and possibly low: relevance filtering of KG context is studied at inference time by the IKG/KGSweetSpot work, so novelty depends entirely on applying selection to the training supervision signal and on the matched-budget curve. Should be positioned as a component of modification 1, not as a standalone contribution, unless the training-time selection dynamics differ demonstrably.

input.why_differs: Differs from the closest work in exactly one defensible way: prior relevance studies operate on prompts at inference (IKG/KGSweetSpot) or choose compact subgraphs by design (DrKGC), whereas this applies selection to the per-example training supervision and reports the precision/recall trade-off as a training-time ablation.

input.description: Insert a failure-attribution stage before any corrective-example generation. Using controlled perturbations on the KG and question pipeline, classify each failing instance into (i) incorrect base fact, (ii) entity-linking/retrieval failure, (iii) composition/shortcut failure. Run the repair loop only on type-(i) failures and report per-type repair rates, with a full-loop comparison as an ablation. If type (i) does not dominate, replace the repair loop with a retrieval/entity-linking fix or drop the component.

input.experimental_difficulty_basis: Requires building controlled perturbation harnesses (inject false triples, corrupt entity links, add composition depth) and re-running evaluation per perturbation, but each run is cheap relative to LLM fine-tuning.
input.implementation_difficulty_basis: Perturbation harnesses and error-type labels must be built; the existing repair loop then needs to be restricted to a failure subset.
input.main_risk: Perturbation-injected errors may not match naturally occurring errors, so the attribution taxonomy could be an artefact of the perturbations. Validating on naturally failing instances (with manual or model-assisted labels) is needed.
input.potential_novelty: Hedged: error-type taxonomies exist elsewhere in QA, but no retrieved multi-hop KGQA work reports per-type repair rates under perturbations, so this is plausibly a first for this sub-area and is useful even if the repair loop is refuted.
input.technical_mechanism: Build perturbation variants of the KG and questions; fit the model on each and label failures by construction. For natural failures, classify with a rule-based/marker-based detector (e.g. whether a wrong intermediate entity vs. a wrong topic-entity link is implicated), then generate corrective examples only for base-fact failures and measure per-type repair rate and collateral harm.

input.why_differs: NSM addresses missing intermediate supervision rather than diagnosing failure types; GNN-RAG names entity-linking failure as a limitation but does not attribute or repair errors. input.description: Treat the ability to use supplied context as a trainable skill, not a free by-product of more tokens. input.main_risk: Position-robustness training may trade away peak in-context accuracy, and the effect may be confounded with data augmentation volume; the augmented arms need matched augmentation budgets.
